summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Eli Langer, a Canadian visual artist born in 1967 in Montreal. It describes how Langer rose to prominence in 1993 with a solo exhibition at the Mercer Union Gallery in Toronto. The show was raided by Toronto police under new child pornography legislation, which sparked a national debate over legal limits and freedom of expression.
one_line: Canadian visual artist Eli Langer, whose 1993 Mercer Union Gallery exhibition was police-raided and sparked a national free-expression debate.
key_facts: Eli Langer was born in 1967 in Montreal, Quebec.
Eli Langer is a Canadian visual artist.
Eli Langer rose to prominence in 1993, at age 26, in the Toronto art world.
Langer's breakthrough was a solo exhibition at the Mercer Union Gallery in Toronto.
The exhibition consisted of 8 paintings and 50 drawings.
The works addressed various issues of childhood sexuality.
Toronto police raided the Mercer Union exhibition under Canada's new child pornography legislation.
Police seized 5 paintings and 35 drawings from the exhibition.
The raid and ensuing media coverage created a national debate.
The national debate concerned the reach of law and freedom of expression.
